title: drEryk says unauthorized access to its systems may affect eRejestracja users
summary: drEryk, a Polish provider of software for medical facilities, says it identified and confirmed unauthorized access to its IT systems on 23 November and cut off the compromised server. Its security notice says the incident may involve eRejestracja users: facility IP address and name, NIP, REGON and patients' PESEL numbers. The company says its analysis is ongoing and it has not yet determined which users are affected.
plain: A Polish medical-software company, drEryk, says someone got into its systems. It says patients' PESEL numbers of eRejestracja users may be involved, and it is still working out who is affected.
exec: drEryk says eRejestracja customers may be affected, and it advises facilities to assess whether to report to the data protection authority (UODO).
action: drEryk advises facilities to revoke P1 certificates immediately, assess individually whether to report to the UODO President, consider notifying patients, and watch for suspicious emails, SMS and calls.

validation.note: drEryk's own security notice and board statement, plus Cyberdefence24 relaying the company's notice.
